question.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-1)\,i+\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\,j+(t-1)\,k$ at the point corresponding to $t=2,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
question.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=2$,  the vector ${r}^{′}(2)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

$$
R(u)=r(2)+u{r}^{′}(2),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

First, we find $r(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =({2}^{2}-1)\,i+\sqrt{1+{2}^{2}}\,j+(2-1)\,k \\  & =3\,i+\sqrt{5}\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,k \\  & =2t\,i+\frac{t}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(2) & =2(2)\,i+\frac{(2)}{\sqrt{1+(2)^{2}}}\,j+\,k \\  & =4\,i+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\,j+\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point 
 where $t=2$ is 

$$
R(u)=3i+\sqrt{5}\,j+\,k+u(4\,i+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\,j+\,k),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
